sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

NC: 2025:KHC:19201 HC-KAR 3. F.I.R. in Crime No.69/2025 was registered by Tumakuru Town Police Station, Tumakuru for the aforesaid offences against the petitioner and four other persons based on the first information dated 29.01.2025 received from Siddalingappa L., S/o Late Lingadevaru.

During the course of investigation of the said case, petitioner herein was arrested on 01.02.2025 and bail application filed by him before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.412/2025 was rejected on 02.04.2025, therefore he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that petitioner is aged about 73 years having no criminal antecedents.

sentences.text: Accused No.2 who was arrested in the present case was granted regular bail by the jurisdictional Court and accused Nos.3 to 5 have been granted anticipatory bail.

Investigation of the case is not completed and chargesheet has not been filed in the present case and therefore petitioner is entitled NC: 2025:KHC:19201 HC-KAR for statutory bail as provided under Section 187 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
Accordingly he prays to allow the petition.

5. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the petition on the ground that there are several allegations made against the petitioner, but he does not dispute the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
6.

In the first information which is filed on 29.01.2025 it is alleged by the first informant that he is a retired government servant and he purchased jewellery from the shop of the petitioner known as Akash Jewellers situated at Tumkur.

It is alleged that the petitioner had represented to the first information that if investments are made for purchase of gold, investors would be getting higher returns and therefore the first informant allegedly consulted with his family members and had thereafter invested totally a sum of Rs.1 crore with the petitioner NC: 2025:KHC:19201 HC-KAR herein for the period from 11.10.2021 to 15.09.2023.
In the first information itself it is mentioned that the petitioner had paid a sum of Rs.6 lakhs to the first informant towards the profit made by the investments during the aforesaid period.

It is alleged that subsequently when the first informant had asked the petitioner to repay the money deposited by him, he had evaded his phone calls and when he went near his jewellery shop, he found that the shop was closed and thereafter on enquiry the first informant learnt that even the house of the petitioner was closed.
It is under these circumstances the first informant had approached the police.
Undisputedly, accused No.2 who was arrested in the present case has been granted regular bail and accused Nos.3 to 5 have been granted anticipatory bail.
So far as the petitioner who is aged 73 years is concerned, he is in custody from 01.02.2025.
Learned HCGP on instructions submits that investigation of the case is not completed and chargesheet is yet to be filed.

The petitioner is in custody from NC: 2025:KHC:19201 HC-KAR 01.02.2025 and in view of Section 187(3)(i) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, since chargesheet is not filed within 90 days from the date of remand of the petitioner to the judicial custody, he is entitled for statutory bail.
Therefore, without going into the merits and demerits of the case, the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of bail is required to be answered in the affirmative.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The petition is allowed.
